note: Example data: an invented home and small-business solar installer, not a real business. Click IDs, lead ids and account ids are made up. Every number in expected_output.json follows from this input.
request: Our Google, Microsoft and Meta ads bring plenty of quote requests, but sales says most never book a site survey. Set up offline conversions so the ad platforms learn which leads turn into customers.

business.name: Example Solar Installers (invented example)
business.sells: rooftop solar and batteries for homes and small businesses, sold after a site survey and a written proposal

crm_export.source: Google Sheets export of the CRM, read with get_sheet_peak and query_sheet_data
notes: original_source comes from the CRM's own website tracking cookie, which works on every page.

The site's current script copies click IDs from the page URL into the form when it is submitted. The contact form is one page. The quote calculator is a three-step form, and its steps 2 and 3 load new pages without the query string. Calls get their click ID from CallRail.
The CRM stores gclid, msclkid and fbclid. It has no fields for gbraid, wbraid, a click timestamp or the GA4 client id.
Times are in the account time zone.
